newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed in volatile trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed in volatile trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed slightly higher on Wednesday in a nervous session dominated by trading on the part of options speculators, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 0.81 percent, or 2.05 points, to 255.82 on a low all-share turnover of 106 million shekels against 92 million shekels on Tuesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.10 percent higher at 263.38.

"Trading was very volatile today. The Maof rose by 1.5 percent but then it started falling, wiping out early gains," said Amir Eayal of Epsilon Securities. "I believe that the main reason was heavy trading by Maof options speculators."
"The market is waiting. It needs to digest the new price level. It rose sharply then it consolidated and now it's waiting for fresh news," Eayal added.
But Dan Lallouz, portfolio manager at Clal Insurance, said he did not believe the market would be turning higher for some time.
"Activity continues to be very low and the market does not look too good," he said. "I think the market will continue to decline after the release of the fourth-quarter earnings reports."

"Now it's time to take profits. Their is no reason for a further rise. In the next few months I believe that the downward trend will continue although in the long run the market will resume its rise," Lallouz said.

The most active shares were Koor Industries, which fell 1.0 percent to 31,763 agorot on volume of 6.8 million shekels; Clal Israel, which closed unchanged at 98 agorot on turnover of 3.9 million shekels; and Bank Hapoalim, which lost 0.5 percent to 651 agorot on volume of 3.2 million shekels.
